title: A machine-learning correction improves two-to-six-week weather forecasts
friendlyTitle: A new method may make longer weather forecasts more accurate
summary: A Nature paper published on 14 October describes probabilistic bias correction, a method that learns to fix systematic errors in existing weather models rather than replacing them. Applied to European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts systems, the authors report better skill for most temperature and precipitation targets at the two-to-six-week range.
friendlySummary: Researchers published a way to correct known errors in existing weather models. They report better forecasts for many temperature and rain targets two to six weeks ahead.
whyItMatters: Forecasts that far ahead matter for planting, energy and storm preparation, where today's models often fade. The paper is open access, but turning a research result into a local operational forecast is still a separate step.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Longer forecasts help farmers, energy planners and emergency teams. This is a research result, not yet a new forecast app on your phone.
